key_insight: Combining structured EHR features, clinical-text embeddings, and knowledge-grounded entity extraction improved sensitivity for 30-day diabetes readmission prediction, but slightly reduced AUROC.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help identify more patients who may be readmitted, though its low specificity would generate substantial false-positive alerts.
method: Fuse engineered EHR features with 32 compressed Bio_ClinicalBERT embedding components.
Extract symbolic entities using hybrid retrieval, cross-encoder re-ranking, and negation auditing.
Predict readmission with cost-sensitive XGBoost and a threshold calibrated using Youden’s J.
evidence_signal: On a patient-grouped held-out test set of 20,153 encounters, sensitivity rose from 0.5839 to 0.6667 and Brier score improved from 0.1080 to 0.0977, while AUROC fell from 0.6477 to 0.6375.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish external or prospective validation, and the provenance of the clinical notes and 500-note Hinglish benchmark needs clarification.
paper_title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
